sources.entry: SQLPage - SQL-only dynamic website builder. (Source Code) MIT Rust/Docker

summary.one_liner: SQLPage is an SQL-only web server that turns `.sql` files and database queries into data-driven websites with tables, forms, charts, and lists.
summary.what_it_does: SQLPage runs as a single executable web server that handles requests to `.sql` URLs by executing the matching SQL file against a connected database. Query result columns are mapped to parameters of pre-built UI components (list, chart, form, card, text, tab, and others) and streamed to the browser as HTML. Users write SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE queries, and form values arrive as SQL parameters such as $first_name. It supports SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, Microsoft SQL Server, and any ODBC-compatible database. Custom components can be added as Handlebars templates, and HTTPS can be enabled with a domain setting.
use_cases: build a data dashboard from a SQL database
create CRUD forms over existing tables
display database query results as charts and tables
prototype an internal tool without a frontend framework
build a simple web app with user login and file uploads
import CSV data into a database through a web form
deploy a small website on AWS Lambda or Docker
how_to_run: Create a file called index.sql with the example contents from the README
Download the release binary for your OS, extract it with: tar -xzf sqlpage-*.tgz
Run it: ./sqlpage.bin (from the folder containing your .sql files)
On macOS: brew install sqlpage, then run sqlpage from your website folder
stack: ODBC (unixODBC on Linux and macOS binaries)
notable: Pages are written entirely as SQL queries, with components selected by a 'component' column
Supports SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, and ODBC databases such as DuckDB, Snowflake, and BigQuery
Built-in HTTP/2 and automatic HTTPS certificates via SQLPAGE_HTTPS_DOMAIN
Can be compiled to an AWS Lambda function, with SQL files optionally stored inside the database
Custom components via .handlebars templates in sqlpage/templates
caveats: Release binaries cover Linux and Windows on x86_64 and macOS on Apple silicon; Intel Macs are told to use Homebrew or build from source
Docker's raw image is stripped down, so the README advises building a custom image on a Debian base for extra dependencies
ODBC databases require installing the database-specific driver separately
The README mentions a managed hosting option (DataPage) and a paid VPS partner offer, which are not part of the open-source project
keywords: build a web form from a table
plots tables and forms from sql
